review:
[h1] WHY IS NO ONE TALKING ABOUT THIS GAME? [/h1]

I could never understand why nobody recommends or talks about this game, which scored 86 on Metacritic. I had a lot of fun while playing it, and it managed to become one of my favorite games.

[h1] Story and Characters - The Road from Accusation to Legend [/h1]

In the story, we control Trigger, who is silent but a legend in the skies. The beginning of the game is quite striking: with the allegation that we accidentally shot our former president (aka 'Ex-President Killer'), we are discharged from the military and condemned to a military prison... In short, the story covers Trigger's transformation from a "scapegoat" into the "Invincible Pilot" everyone relies on. We experience our real rise when they start attacking the prison. We are sent to the 444th Air Base (Spare Squadron), where convict pilots are held. Together with the convict pilots there, we jump into whatever planes we have and try to protect the prison and its surroundings. Of course, thanks to the legendary Trigger, we complete this mission successfully. Our success in this mission draws attention and serves as a notice for new missions. Once our innocence is learned, we rejoin an elite unit (Strider Squadron). Naturally, other friends we met in prison also join here. As we succeed in missions, our reputation spreads everywhere before we even arrive. The Three Strikes: harbinger of death for enemies, symbol of hope for allies. Over time, everyone starts respecting Trigger and taking refuge behind him.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails?id=3687024972
The story isn't just about action. In the background, the hardships faced by civilians, the refugees we are tasked with protecting, and even the family ties of the rivals we fight deepen the narrative. It makes you feel that the war is not just between two nations, but taking place among innocent people who bear no blame. In the finale, with that famous “space elevator” and narrow tunnel sections, we prove to the whole world why Trigger is a living legend.

[h1] Gameplay and Mechanics [/h1]

Ace Combat 7 is not a simulation. Even though plane models are identical to real life, their maneuverability pushes the laws of physics. In addition, there are plane designs that do not exist in real life. But are these downsides? Never! This arcade nature of the game makes dogfights much smoother and more fun. After all, don't we all play games to have fun? AC7 delivers this fun to the fullest.

Missions are generally successful. One moment we are chasing enemies through stormy mountains, and the next we are conducting an infiltration mission below 600 meters without being detected by radar. The best part is that the atmosphere and location of most missions are different places. Even though the final chapters take place in similar locations due to the story, it doesn't get boring thanks to the fun gameplay. That famous narrow tunnel sequence and the space elevator climb in the finale... I failed 3-4 times while flying through the narrow tunnel. I might have also died 1-2 more times while flying up the space elevator... Dying is inevitable for beginners to flight mechanics and gameplay like me. No matter how hard it is, it is worth the sense of satisfaction when we succeed.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails?id=3685557980
I also have to say that the game is not flawless. The only part—or rather mission design—that bored me was the missions where we grind points while racing against time. Doing these missions back-to-back with short intervals started to bore me a bit, but luckily they kept these missions to a minimum and didn't disrupt the gameplay pacing. Because constantly hitting ground targets becomes extremely boring and annoying after a point.

[h1] Graphics and Atmosphere [/h1]

The graphics are simply magnificent. Moisture droplets forming on the cockpit when flying into clouds, electronics glitching when struck by lightning, and the sun reflecting off our wings take the atmosphere to the top. The fact that each chapter has its own unique geography and weather keeps the game visually fresh. At the same time, it maintains the gameplay pacing.

[h1] Music and Sound Effects [/h1]

Sound design is one of the most important factors enhancing the atmosphere. The roar of the engine, the missile lock-on sound, and radio chatter echoing in the headset connect us to the game wonderfully. The music is exactly as it should be. Thrilling, and it hypes us up with every maneuver.

An example of the game's music:
https://youtu.be/XWDdpaQYoA4

[h1] Technical and Performance [/h1]

Technically, it is quite a stable game. Thanks to smooth FPS rates and fast loading times, the action is never interrupted.

[h1] Overall  [/h1]

I like fighter jets, but I had never played a fighter jet game before. A title capable of turning someone with zero interest in airplanes into a lover of the skies. With the good story it offers, unforgettable final sequences, and a protagonist like Trigger, it definitely deserves to be played. I've already wishlisted Ace Combat 8 and am waiting for it. It drops to $4 during sales; you should definitely give it a chance.

So, do you want to become an ace or what?

Let me get this right  out of the way, its an arcade flying game, not a simulator, if you are looking for a hardcore flying sim, look elsewhere. Its also hard for me to give this game an honest review, because I absolutely loved it and enjoyed every minute I spent with it, but Ill try to be fair and not forget any flaws this game had. 

First things first, sadly an important thing these days, the technical side of things: its pretty much flawless, it runs great and is definently well optimized, the FPS is unlocked and reaching 200+ fps is not uncommon with this game and trust me, flying at 144hz and above feels absolutely awesome, the game never ever crashed in all my time spent with it, nor did i ever have to kill its process, it never locked up my system or anything and I honestly cant recall any bugs with it, at all, in 2019, thats quite an achievement compared to other AAA games. The graphics and effects are all great and a real eye candy, no complaints there. The sound is on point, be it explosions, your aicraft or your weapons. The soundtrack itself is great and by the way, the english dub is absolutely solid, which is not a given for a japanese game.

Gameplay? Well its simply put - fun as hell, you fly around, pull off some impressive aerobatics while blowing stuff up! Flying targets, ground targets, sea targets, moving or stationary, you name it, you gonna be blowing it all up! The game tries to add a bit of variety to it, like flying through a canyon or avoiding radar detection, staying under clouds in a rocky area, guiding rockets of bombers or searching for targets in a sandstorm or just a regular rain storm and so on, but at the end of the day, for the most of it, you gonna be blowing stuff up, be it to save your comrades or just to achieve some highscore, you gonna be blowing a lot of stuff up and with a great variety of weapons and planes, both imaginary and real, its definently a blast to play.

The story is actually alright, I mean its not flawless and can get you confused at first, because of cutscenes following both your friends and your enemies and requiring you to know at least a bit of past ace games, the story is still fine but the most important bit of it, you are at the center of it all. You are a faceless voiceless protagonist like gordon freeman, but the game plays with it pretty well, you are adressed via your callsign that changes as the story progresses and thats not the only thing that changes. You start off as a nobody, a newbie fighter pilot and you finish the game as an ace of aces, a legendary pilot and everyones favourite. The game does a great job of making you feel like THE ace. Ground troops cheer for you when they see you flying over them and giving air support and promise to buy beer later, your wingmen and wingwomen salute your skill and react to your performance on the battlefield, the enemies start to panic when they see your arrival. I gotta be honest, it made me feel pretty good while playing it. The game centers around the "man vs machine" theme, fighter pilots vs drones, so it feels pretty modern and relevant to our world. So overall I enjoyed it, even after replaying the game 5 times now.

But no game is without a flaw and this game is no exception, Ace Combat 7 is very much a singleplayer centered game, while there is multiplayer its a rather simple deathmatch mode and thats about it, there are no great battles to fight with or against your friends. My biggest letdown was lack of any sort of co-op mode, most if not all missions in the game could easily be made into co-op and as we all know, anything is even more fun with friends, not saying that the game is boring as it is, but blowing stuff up with a friend or two would not hurt it. The singleplayer itself is a bit short, you can probably finish it in about 11 to 13 hours, so for people looking for a looooong story, I am afraid its not the case here, still I enjoyed replaying those several times to clock over 70 hours in it, as previously mentioned, the variety of both weapons and aircrafts helps to keep it fresh as you try new toys in the same missions.

So my overall verdict? Its an awesome arcady fly and shoot type of game, that is fairly easy to get into for anyone new to the genre, its well worth your time and money, but I would not recommend buying it at full price due to just not enough content to justify the 60$/€ price tag, but 40% off and below? I would say go for it, you won't regret that you got it and you will have a great time. And by the by, its not like there is any other better or even just good alternative on the market, with other ace games only being available on consoles and ubisofts HAWX series being dead for a while now. As far as DLC goes, its reasonably priced, the 3 additional missions and 3 aircrafts are all great, so you only have to ask yourself if you want more or you are content with the base game.

Because I had heard that the composer of this game also worked some stuff in Uma Musume (another title that I got into thanks to the music). But I did not expect to get attached to the characters and get invested in the story. With Count, Tabloid, Wiseman, Long Caster, and even Bandog being some of my favorites. Though I will say, I wish they'd actually help you with the mission instead of basically just being flies on the battlefield.
Not to mention the over-the-top set pieces actually made me hyped, not cringe. That, and combined with the OST? Heavenly.

I went into the Ace Combat series completely blind, I had never played any of the previous games. 
[b]I am so glad I bought this, even without knowing anything about the series. [/b] 
I've beat every mission at least 4 times (For the Hardened Vet achievement) So I think I'm now qualified to write this review. 

This game gets you into the seat of a fighter within the first 10 minutes. Following a 5 minute cutscene that introduces you to a character you will follow (through cut-scenes and a couple missions)  as you progress through the main story. (And also a really well done briefing that you will have before each mission.) Every element of the first 10 minutes of this game are there to acclimate you to the story and objectives you'll face. 

Gameplay consists of fighting land, sea and air based targets, with either your machine gun, or missiles, and special weapon types. These can range from guided/unguided bombs, to specialized rockets/missiles, even railguns. All while you expertly pilot your craft taking down enemies, the most common threat is SAM missiles and drones. Drones are a common enemy, and the story revolves around the consequence of their use in the skies and in war.  

Jets are accurately recreated in stunning quality and every flap, every turn, every pull of the trigger. is carefully tuned to give you the feeling that you ARE in control. Contrails, condensation on the glass, ice, clouds forming around wings as you pull high G turns. 

First person is extremely immersive, allowing you to pilot through the clouds as if you were actually in the cockpit.
Whether it be an F-22, or any other of the many faithfully made jets the game has to offer. 
Third person brings you a broader perspective of the fighting in the skies around you. You can also use your controller or keyboard to follow targets while you control the craft, creating epic shots as you loop around in the most stunning way possible. 

You are a silent protagonist going by the name of Trigger. 90% of the time you will hear characters talking through radio, either to you or with other characters. As you progress through the game you will join different fighter groups and are attached to an AWACS. These AWACS (Airborne Warning and Control Systems) are characters with diverse personality and dialogue that match your current circumstance. It doesn't end there however. Every bit of dialogue is perfectly timed to match up visually in game, such as a jet crashing or a character meeting an untimely end. enemy and allied units will interact/progress as you do, creating a sense that every objective you complete [b]Actually matters.[/b]  

In short, this review was poorly constructed, but I hope it illustrates how much this game means to me. I also hope it convinces you that this game truly is worth all your time and money. My review does not do this game justice, there's so much to love you just can't walk away. You have to experience the Skies Unknown yourself. : )

Before this, the only Ace Combat game I had played was Assault Horizon long ago. I remember liking it and not understanding why it got the hate it did. So when I saw this game on sale, I decided to get it. From the moment I lifted off the the runway in that 1st mission, hearing that soundtrack, it felt like something in my soul was healing. A joy I didn't know still existed within me burst forth.

As I played the game, I reach a mission about 1/3 of the way into the game and it kicked my butt. I started to think it was impossible as I just couldn't do it. I even looked up a video online of someone beating the level, looking for some sort of secret I was missing, there wasn't one. I just had to get good. So that's what I did. I buckled down in the game and just kept trying, kept flying, kept getting just a little bit better each time. By the time I reached the end of the game, I felt like I truly was an Ace. The previous mission in which it took me 10 tries to get the 15,000 points to beat, I now regularly go back to and effortlessly get over 50,000. There is no secret to beating this game besides sticking with it and getting good, but when you do get good at it, you will feel like you're flying. Not flying a plane, just, flying.

The DLC missions are also top notch as some of the best missions in the game, with great music, objectives, and enemy aces.

Can't recommend this game highly enough, especially if you see it on sale. Remember, stick with Trigger, and you'll make it.

If you like me, saw the Ace Combat 8 trailer and had never heard of this game before, I wouldn't blame you. I had no idea what I was walking into but for £3.99, it was worth a try. 

GOOD. LORD. 

This game is incredible. I was expecting to just mess around shooting a few planes and that would be that. Somehow, each mission becomes more complex and gives you something new to think about. The story is compelling enough to continue on and care about the characters and your voiceless character has an entire arc of their own. 

The best part of this game, by far, is the sound design. The music is powerful and matches the pace of the action. If you have ever played any Metal Gear Solid game and enjoyed the cinematic style of music, this is the game for you. Even if you haven't ever played a game like this before (I hadn't), you will likely love this game. 

Brilliant value when on sale but honestly, I would pay more for such a strong game.

I really enjoyed it but now that I'm done the campaign I feel like there's nothing left to do since I don't really enjoy pvp. I wish there was a solo or even co-op arcade mode or wave survival mode. I'd play the heck out of that kind of mode in this type of game.

I'm not really good at writing reviews, but I'll try to sum up my thoughts on this game. 

Ace Combat 7 has been an absolute blast to play through. I'm currently about 3 quarters of the way into my run on Hard Difficulty, and despite that I'm still having an absolute blast. The game is fairly challenging, but not overbearing. I've crashed more than a few times, and despite that, I keep coming back no matter how pissed off I get at myself. The multiplayer has also been a good time, and dogfighting my buddies has been even better. The planes and environment are quite well detailed, and I've never had a moment where I would consider the game ugly. The soundtrack is one of the best I've ever had the pleasure of listening to, and it really helps to get me motivated, in game, or IRL. 

I think if you like these sorts of flight arcade games, you'll love Ace Combat 7. It's been an absolute blast, and I am thrilled to see what comes next.

I played this game on the PS4 first. 2019 was a phenomenal year for video games, unparalleled in the prior two decades, and this is yet another game that made it so.

You may have missed this release amidst the flurry of other releases. This is understandable. I forgive you. But if you did, you need to correct that mistake. You owe it to yourself, and you owe it to me.

Ace Combat has always been one of the greatest series in the medium. Ace Combat 3 will never be brought over to the West, and that's a pain I live with for the rest of my life. Ace Combat 4 brought a masterfully-made keen sadness to war for the first time I know of in any sort of flight game. Within so short a time we went from Gradius to philosophical reflection on the cruelty of war.

Ace Combat 5 was pretty good. The soundtrack is better than the game.

Ace Combat 0 may be the greatest video game of all time. And that's why you owe me. Because not enough people bought Ace Combat 0, or 6, and then we had to suffer in the dark, suffer in the grim despair of knowing that all we were ever going to get anymore was Assault Horizon and a cash grab online-only scam game.

This was the pit in which we happy few who got to enjoy this series in its prime were doomed to wallow in, right until Ace Combat 7 brought back most of what we wanted. Most of what was missing in life.

Ace Combat 7 is not the ultimate game of this series - that title is still held by 0, depending on your priorities. But it is a phenomenal portrayal of the foolishness of modern warfare, it is a stark analysis of the contrast between how nations portray themselves and how they truly are. It's a political drama whose focal characters kind of suck sometimes. But that's okay.

It's about the creeping advance on technology, and also a love letter to its own series in so many ways. Ace Combat 7 is the game we needed, and there needs to be an 8th game. I need you to understand that this game is really good, REALLY good. There's a lot of changes. The targeting ring from 0 is gone and I sorely miss its absence. There is ONE mission that sucks a ton. (Sandstorm....) And one of the POV characters I wanted off the screen whenever they were on the screen.

But that's the sum total downsides. So what are the upsides? What joy does this bring to your life? Why will you be better off for having played this?

The planes feel amazing. Cockpit view is as stellar as ever. The music is exactly what it should be. The scales of battles have never been larger, the AI is massively more competent than ever before (this game on Normal is sometimes harder than Ace Combat 0 was on Ace) and the story despite a handful of stumbling points remains a heartwrenching bitter tale of overcoming the worst parts of humanity. Of triumph in the face of despair.

You will not regret buying and playing this game. And you will join me in wanting a port of Ace Combat 0 to something more modern than the PS2 so you, too, can enjoy it for what it is: a masterpiece.

Ace Combat 7 is a 9/10 excellent game, and if I convince enough of you to buy it we might one day get another 12/10 like Zero. Join me in rejoicing at the glorious return of a series so many thought was dead and gone forever.

[h1] First of all, what's the game like? [/h1]
Well, this is a great option for [spoiler] you maverick wannabes [/spoiler] air combat lovers who want to have a good time other than war thunder and dcs. Mechanics are simple to understand and the overall sceneries in the game are just splendid. And particularly the soundtracks ingame [spoiler] hail to Kobayashi-san [/spoiler] are incredibly phenomenal, which every game throughout the entire franchise possesses, they will not let you down.

[h1] About the Singleplayer... [/h1]
[b] The base game [/b]
The lore is okay-ish, storytelling is fine [strike] hey at least you got a pretty nice looking waifu [/strike] and it's not very hard to figure out the whole background and it's totally not a problem if you haven't played any of the previous games. The missions are time limited and can be a challenge if you are new to the game, with more practice you won't have any difficulties dealing with them [strike] yes you can speedrun the whole game[/strike] . Almost every different weapon in the game offers a unique playstyle, you can focus heavy strike on a single target with highly maneuverable QAAMs, or getting rid of a large enemy group with 4/6/8AAMs. The game almost offers a varieties of futuristic weapons like the Tactical Laser System [strike] an onboard laserpointer [/strike], the EML [strike] basically a railgun [/strike], MPBMs [strike] multipurpose tactical nukes ;) [/strike] and so on. Some of the missions provides special mechanics [spoiler] contains but not limited to: low altitude breakthrough/valley runs/gigantic super weapons/tUnNels [/spoiler] which add more fun to the campaign.
[b] The DLC missions [/b]
Definitely worth the price, has another huge air to air only combat apart from the base campaign, more mechanics and adds a fantastic and attractive villain, play it yourself for the best experience.
[b] The mods [/b]
Yes this game supports modding and oh boy, the communities are just went all out. You can have completely new aircrafts with new weapons from iconic aircrafts in previous titles or aircrafts in real life, new hud, new effects, new skins for aircrafts and even maps with a completely different setting. Apart from those you can also have rebalanced AIs which gives you a more challenging campaign and new mechanics which tweak from the aircraft cannon firerates to new missile tracking methods. Still, i recommend trying the mods out after at least finishing the original campaign once.

[h1] About the Multiplayer... [/h1]
[u] PLEASE DO PLAY THE SINGLEPLAYER FIRST BEFORE TRYING MP [/u]
[b] Overall situation [/b]
This is where all things went down, only two game modes are available and they are max 8 players free for alls and max    4v4 team death match. Apart from those two you can also set for 1v1 games but it's really time consuming if you want to get your skills up. Also, many experienced players wander around and they will not give you a good time in MP and can easily ruin your experience and make you ragequit, [i] Seriously, you have been warned [/i], prepare for being killed over and over again if you are rookies to the game. [spoiler] Stay away from those lobbies with "join midmatch" turned off and theres only one player in it, you will most likely get rekt very hard. [/spoiler]
[b] Mechanics [/b]
For battle royals [spoiler] not the one you expected [/spoiler] or free for all is competing for the best, the match ends when anyone reaches 100k score. For team death matches, mostly are the same as the battle royal mode except the game ends when any of the teams reaching 250k score. In both game modes, if a player got a score thats high enough, he would receive stars varying from 1 to 3, which in turn maximum triples the scores you get from killing them. Remember to configure your aircraft set in the hangar first before entering any match or you will be end up on a stock F16. Inside the hanger you get access to different parts that can boost your aircrafts and weapons performance dramatically, but the slots and options are limited so be wise on your loadout.
[b] Some warnings [/b]
Be very mentally prepared before entering MP, it's P2P based so connection quality will impact your experience a lot. Furthermore, the game has NO anti cheat methods and it's very painful when encountering one. A point worth mentioning is that a lot of the advanced techniques, for instance backwards flying [spoiler] yes you see that correct, flying literally backwards not upside down [/spoiler] would behave very similar to cheating but they are different fundamentally.

[h1] TL;DR[/h1]
Good game if you like arcade flying with exciting combats, the SP part is around 30 hours with many content, mods add a lot more fun to the game and theres plenty of them, the MP experience is basically trash if you are not willing to spend time taking hits and sharping your skills and learning stuff. Not worth the full price, get it when on discount.

Ace Combat 7 is a game about melodramatic fighter pilots, conspiracies, the moral implications of drone warfare, and staying conscious at levels of G-Force that logically should probably make your brain leak out of your ears. If that sounds intriguing, read on.

After playing Project Wingman (An excellent title I cannot recommend enough) for the first time, I decided to explore the Ace Combat series in greater depth, having previously only played Assault Horizon, the oft-discussed black sheep entry of the series. Since that time I have played the Playstation 2 "Holy Trinity", and now this most recent, multiplatform entry. 

For those unfamiliar, Ace Combat is set in the constructed world of "Strangereal", and the name says it all: A world not unlike ours, with a patchwork of nations and an equivalent level of technology... with very specific exceptions. While the people of Strangereal are far more vahemently opposed to the construction and use of nuclear weapons then us, a deadly asteroid impact only a few decades prior to the events of the series prompted accelerated development of alternative superweapons in the interest of repelling future impacts. Many of these form the basis for the spectacle-inducing boss fights that, together with its relatively lax physics and hyperspace ammunition pools, set Ace Combat apart from more realism-focused flight sims of yesteryear, like the Jane's series.

Perhaps due to the lack of nuclear deterrence, international, conventional combined-arms conflicts happen alarmingly often in this universe, and this time its the "Lighthouse War", a struggle to control this world's only space elevator and the gateway to humanity's future. You are Trigger, a pilot in the Osean air force- the same nation depicted in detail in AC5. Your opponents are the forces of Erusea- the same foes from AC4. Skies Unknown has a lot of callbacks to these two games in particular. As with most series protagonists, Trigger is a faceless mute that nonetheless gains a fearsome reputation over the course of the campaign.

Skies Unknown presents a variety of aesthetic and mechanical improvements over its predecessors, but I think falls short of Ace Combat 5: The Unsung War and moreso Project Wingman in terms of writing, voicework and characterization. Project Wingman also has far superior music and a certain charm not found here, though that hardly makes Skies Unknown a bad game by comparison. It is if nothing else a very pretty game, thanks to Unreal engine.

I mentioned some improvements to the gameplay: New to the series is a tech tree not only featuring new aircraft for purchase but passive upgrades with varying effects and equip costs. A given plane can equip up to eight of these mods and higher-tier planes have less total capacity, meaning they may not be able to equip the same set of mods. AC7 features online multiplayer and I'm sure this is a balancing measure for that reason. Also, and I think this was a feature earlier in the series (though not in any of the ones i've played), you can perform a "High-G" Turn by holding both your thrust and brake buttons at the same time, though this will cause you to quickly lose speed and easily stall your plane if you're not careful. Aggressive use of High-G turns is necessary for basically any mission after the first, and especially against the bosses. More so then almost any game I've played, Ace Combat 7 put a severe strain on my fingers and arms. You may wish to employ compression gloves like me, or some other physical aid.

Ace Combat 7 is also on the whole more difficult and intense then both its predecessors or Project Wingman. I found myself restarting levels and crashing into the ground significantly more often then those other games. There is an additional "Very Easy" difficulty, and I think this game's "Normal" is equivalent to "Hard" In the PS2 games. It wasn't hard enough to be really annoying, but enough to be immersion-breaking. AC7 has higher flight speeds, more evasive enemy aces, and what feels like larger enemy groups overall.

If you enjoy arcade air combat, AC7 is worth a look, especially at the steep discounts it typically gets during sales. just be aware that its not exactly a casual experience and I wouldn't worry about playing it a lower difficulty then you are accustomed to.

This game is an unexpected gem. I never played an Ace Combat game before and picked this up on a sale, thinking nothing of it.

It's not a flight simulator - it's an action game, with just a pinch of sophistication. Jumping into the series at this point I had no context for the story and was utterly unable to understand it (it's standard-fare, absolutely-impossible-Japanese-anime-drama), but fortunately this did not get in the way of me enjoying the game at all. And what a game it is!

The action is [i]on point[/i]. You tear across the sky in one of many choices of jet aircraft, unleashing gratuitous numbers of missiles at your enemies. Mission variety is incredible as you take on one objective after another in a constantly-shifting war. The missions themselves change in the blink of an eye, with unexpected enemy reinforcements showing up mid-fight, VIPs to escort, secret weapon debuts, friendly casualties, and even [i]the weather[/i] forcing you to adapt on-the-fly and overcome. Your wingmen shout encouragement, your enemies scream in terror, the incredible soundtrack swelling and receding with the intensity of combat... once this game grabs you, boredom is [i]impossible.[/i]

I played through the campaign and really enjoyed it - the last couple of missions got somewhat tedious as there are a few sections of artificial difficulty that I was glad to see the end of. Didn't touch multiplayer. The masterful soundtrack stuck in my head for a good week, and it's so good that it lured me back to revisiting the game - something I rarely do these days.

Replaying the campaign with a more thorough understanding of AC7 was exciting all over again. With much more of the game's tech tree now open to me, there is a whole new aspect and art to choosing what to fly and what to equip it with. With more knowledge and a proper loadout, you're not just achieving your objectives - you are now wiping out the entire map of enemies with overwhelming firepower and unholy speed, while new voice lines from the characters draw attention to your mythical prowess.

This is when the magic of AC7's power fantasy truly clicked for me. This game is really well done, and I absolutely recommend you play it.

Let me start of with, as of this review, according to steam, I am one of the 0.3% of players on steam to finish all missions on ACE difficulty at rank S and the 0.1% of players to have obtained at least 25 medals. I have fully played this game and experienced pretty much everything it has to offer.

I have played AC4, AC5 and AC Zero back when it was on the PS2, then AC6 on the Xbox 360 and AC Assault Horizon on the PC. ACE COMBAT 7 is a true sequel to the AC franchise that fans like me have been waiting for. This game will give you the thrill of piloting realistic looking military fighter planes carrying hundreds of missiles, flying at top speed, destroying tons of other fighters planes, military vehicles while performing high-G maneuvers to dodge enemy missiles, AA fire and to dogfight other enemy aces.

Lets start of with the campaign. The campaign is set in the Strangereal universe, the story is told through cutscenes, both outside and in-game, as well as radio chat that you will hear from various characters in game. There are 20 missions in total, you can select various difficulty level to suit you if you are either a new player to the AC series or a veteran. The military style briefing is there at the start of each mission, showcasing what you will be facing up against, so that you can equip your plane loadout accordingly. Each mission is well designed, offering unique challenges with the new cloud and wind system. You will find yourself in missions with sensitive time limit objectives, or trying to dogfight and destroy enemy UAVs which can do crazy high-G maneuvers while flying in thunder clouds, avoiding being struck by lighting which will immobilize your planes and cause you to crash in the mountains, or facing an enemy naval installation and fleet with vast Anti-Air placements and will constantly dodging enemy fire while using special high damage weapons against the enemy.

A point based progression system has been added where you can unlock new planes and weapons to face more challenging enemies in higher difficulties. Upgrades to planes has also been added to enhance your plane in a wide variety, like increased maneuverability or your missile load limit.

On the PC, the controls feels smooth, the framerates are smooth too. The campaign will show you spectacular visuals in the Strangereal universe, the sci-fi superweapons, like the giant drone aircraft carrier, or the massive Anti-Asteroid gun, or futuristic drones with laser weaponry. Missions occur in urban, desert or mountainous regions with day and night time settings. After 53 hours of play, I have not had a single crash, this game is very stable.

There is a lot of replayability and is also where you can see the game at its finest. After completing the campaign once, you will unlock the highest difficulty: ACE. You will want to try to complete each mission with the highest ranking at S, which denotes the best efficiency rating, or try to obtain all the campaign medals, some like completing the entire campaign using only machine guns, or not taking damage once, or completing it under 4 hours, will be challenging. The enemy benefits from the vastly improved AI behavior at increased difficulty which makes gameplay much more fun and challenging. Enemy AA are much more responsive and all AA tanks will start firing at you once you reach missile range. Enemy planes dogfight much more often, and also at much closer range. This allows you to see close up to the enemy planes and much more intense dog fighting moments without needing to resort to the DFM mechanic from AC Assault Horizon. SAMs will fire more frequently and more powerful AAM like those from naval ships or the giant aircraft carrier will fire rapidly. The objectives in the missions will be further emphasized and will be very time sensitive or prone to failure if you dont react quickly. Unlike AC Assault Horizon, there is far less scripting on the enemy bosses. On missions where you can't destroy the enemy boss yet, usually when introducing the boss, its flight movement is half-scripted and half free, it will take you through certain events, although there is no DFM like mechanic at all and you are free to move about and shoot, and the boss will still try to dodge all weapons fire and also fire missiles at you, however, you cant destroy the boss no matter how many times you shoot at it, even with direct weapons like the machine gun. On missions where you can destroy the boss, there is no scripting on its movement and its free movement against it with no cut scenes or interruptions. Enemy bosses also benefits a lot from the improved AI and will perform extreme high-g maneuvers that will match even your top tier planes and will be almost cruel in timing when to fire their missiles that will be hard to dodge like right after you perform your post stall maneuvers and are too slow to move away. To get the S ranking, you will need to destroy your enemies as fast as possible in the shortest amount of time, there is a wide variety of choice of planes to use, each with its own set of special weapons with its own strength. You will need to use upgrades appropriately to upgrades your plane's maneuverability and weapon strength to maximize efficiency, although once you have the points, you will most likely be using the top tier planes only. Going through all missions on ACE difficulty for rank S, you will be flying at top speed, efficiently taking enemies out with missiles, special weapons and machine gun, aiming and timing when to fire your weapons at the right time as you have limited weapon ammo and moving at low speeds to take out as many ground targets at once, while the ground enemy is constantly pumping AA and SAM fire at you and the enemy planes are on your tail firing its missiles and machine guns at you, your HUD is constantly red with the missile alert warning and alarm constantly blaring, performing countless high-g maneuvers to dodge enemy fire and avoid near crash situations, while needing to hear the AWACs updating you on mission objectives and event situations, all while listening to the awesome sound track, and finally succeeding is the most satisfying thing you can experience in AC games that few games can offer.
 
Over on to multiplayer, unlike AC Assault Horizon, it is only plane vs plane in the form of Battle Royal and Team Deathmatch mode, so planes that are multi-role or anti-ground focused will not have much use compared to fighters. However, almost all planes in this game have at least one form of anti-air special weapons which makes very few planes not worth using at all. The way AC games usually work for multiplayer, top tier planes can pretty much evade standard missiles and even special missiles easily. AC Assault Horizon combats this issue with the DFM mechanic, however for AC 7, the upgrade mechanic contains some upgrades that allows you to enhance your missiles homing capabilities greatly, and its only available for multiplayer. This makes it almost impossible to evade missiles unless you travel at high speed and perform high-g maneuvers. This sort of fixes the problem where you will never get a missile hit against a player and have to get a lucky shot. It also makes top tier pvp matches more intense and fast paced. There are new additions to the special weapons which are more skill based. Choosing planes at top tier along with better upgrade parts will create a higher cost point, players can create rooms with custom rules limiting higher cost point planes or disabling the use of special weapons, this makes all the lower tier planes usable and useful.

Overall, ACE COMBAT 7 is a awesome game and a must have for AC fans and a great game for players who enjoy Arcardy-style, fast-paced explosive action-packed fun.

The Ace Combat franchise is literally a fighter pilot power fantasy anime and absurdity is the very definition of such genre. 

The game is fantastic. The gameplay is about as classic as you can get, and the missions do a lot of very interesting things with the formula. The visuals and sound design are outstanding, too. My biggest complaint is with the story, where I never expected there to be this level of chaos and plot holes. A story lives and dies by its characters, and that is where Ace Combat 7 severely lacks in polish. Let me give you a brief synopsis… 

TLDR: Unlucky dude sent over on unwanted desert vacation finds redemption stopping Skynet. Special guest stars: Toni Stark, Nickelback, Falcon and useless Elsa.

A beloved former President gets the authentic Captain Davenport experience because you aren’t his personal air force this time. 

The plot and my synopsis could just end here, but some drooling idiot takes the blame and is forced to fly the Green Mile. He turns out to be too good for solitary cause Mister X can’t give it to him so the token black guy gives him his own squadron, complete with a dad. 

Logan Paul, former lead singer of Nickelback, tags along with the drooling idiot and whines while Guy Fieri looks at a radar and stirs everyone’s appetite with the prospects of Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives. The group goes on a continental trip and participates in an international archeological excavation.

The gang is confronted by Mister X and his friends at the end of their continental trip and the token black guy proves that he is a greater drooling idiot than the drooling idiot himself. The Internet connection suddenly goes out. Anarchy ensues, preventing the group from going home on time. The group makes the most of it and visits an island destination and then an ancient castle where the drooling idiot gives it to Mister X.

Finally, they attend an anti-technology protest with a Disney princess where Logan Paul, former lead singer of Nickelback, redeems himself by being helpful to the drooling idiot. The Internet gets restored by Shadow the Scrap Queen at the end of the protest and everyone gets to go home.

It’s a memorable vacation packed with enough stories to tell your boy about for years.

The basic lessons of Ace Combat’s story is that single or small groups of pilots have a startling tendency to influence the outcomes of major wars, and Belka DID NOTHING WRONG. 

10/10

War is bad but planes are rad. Few things give me as much joy as flying as fast as possible and splashing bandits. The tutorial is good at getting you used to plane games but I definitely recommend sinking in a little time to learn to fly with the expert controls. The story is good if you're looking for that although in some missions it can be a little difficult to tell what's going on story-wise because you're trying to focus on the objective (I'm looking at you Mission 16). You get a wide variety of planes to choose from, with the aircraft tree splitting into three routes, American jets, Russian jets, and EU jets. Getting new planes and armament for those planes can feel a bit overwhelming at first but don't worry about trying to get every plane and just focus on one tree. I will say that I think BamCo is going a little nutso-mode with the DLC for AC7 but I suggest getting the ones that bring DLC missions. All in all, if you like plane games you probably already own this one and if you don't like plane games, wait for it to go on sale and give it a shot.

There is a very real thrill to the motion of a divebomb or an evasive maneuver that this franchise has been capitalizing on for ages now. There is a reason why Ace Combat has been quietly surviving with both a dedicated fanbase and wandering military aviation nerds, that being the fact that this is the furthest thing you can get from some cashgrab simulation flight sim. It's sole focus is making you feel like a mythical fighter pilot from an action movie, and it stops at nothing to make itself into an exciting, tactile, difficult to master celebration of the sheer cool factor that these aircraft have. It's unbelievably well built and good looking as well. With such a simple gameplay loop after all these years, it's like the rest of the game had the room to have an incredibly high bar of quality. The UI is visually stunning and functional, there is an entire livery editor, and the base game planes have enough variety between the three big development trees to warrant a replay or two.

Have you played Armored Core 6? This follows the same formula as that. It's mission based with briefs and debriefs in between. Some missions are simple exercises in dogfighting, but some go absolutely off the rails in how you're challenged or forced into adapting. My personal favorite being a valley run where you have to stay out of sight of guard tower searchlights while navigating the winding terrain under them, just barely managing to slip under bridges and around S curves without crashing.

Learn to love the myth of the ace pilot, nerd out about the real aircraft all of these things take after, and enjoy the thrills that this game has to offer. An unbelievably fun experience.

AC7 is a short and sweet merging of Star Fox and Metal Gear. It's got a great combination of music, art style, mission design, and (for the most part) voice acting. The cinematics are generally good, but very anime. A lot of the voice acting mid-mission can be a tad too much in the over-acting department, but it does make for an entertaining scenario.

There's some very clever mission design here to spice up the traditional air fighter game. Many of the missions do make you feel like a superhero of the skies, with some challenge here and there. Then there are some missions that feel very much out of your league like fighting a chess computer at full strength when you don't understand checkers. I do have a minor gripe with some mission designs where after completing a main part of it, a second part of the mission enables, and you can't change your loadout or resupply your ammo.

The information for you to take in can get overwhelming at times, but I think it fits as a 'type 2' kind of fun. You'll be in a mission, being constantly locked on by missiles, having to dodge repeatedly, while a timer counts down before some calamity happens, while your wingmen and villians blast your radio channels. When you've succeeded, it really feels earned, but sometimes I wish I could mute my friendly pilots.

The soundtrack is great and really hits some good tones of wild cowboy gunning as well as epic opera battle music. The visuals are also stunning from the environments you're in. There's a ton of variety from ice buildups, stormy or dark weather, sunsets, and clear blue skies. 

The DLC is quite good, if a bit more moustache-twirling. If haven't played an Ace Combat game in a million years like I have, give this one a try. But do be warned, there have been episodes of Dragon Ball Z with less anime than this game.

Soundtrack. Very fitting, never found that something was kinda off. In the big "events", there is also epic music to make it more intense which is always nice. Also, the voice actors make the game way more alive.

So, basically, if you have the opportunity to play it, just do it.

Ace Combat 7 is a return to the form of yesteryear.
Bandai Namco did everything they could to make Ace Combat 7 a top title and they succeeded.
The variety in missions is huge and in terms of graphics and audio, Ace Combat 7 is one of the flight combat titles on PC.

Watch a short gameplay here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zrngIJjkrSc

The story is a bit faded, but that won't stop you from getting a lot of fun out of the game.
The length of the missions can vary enormously. There are missions that can be completed in five to ten minutes, but there are also 20 to 25 minutes. It is often difficult to predict in advance how long you will be working on a mission. Fortunately, there are checkpoints. If you make a mistake, you don't have to redo the whole mission. But… these checkpoints are sometimes very far apart.

The game works great on a steam deck too: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=feNkWRXlk0M

Each mission takes place in a different setting, so you're always anxiously awaiting what's to come.
What also makes you want to keep playing this game are the graphics and the sound.
You really often stand with your mouth open looking at the fantastically designed aircraft, the various types of terrain and the clouds.
Dynamic weather conditions sound nice on the back of the packaging, but the great thing is that it really adds something in Ace Combat 7. When you fly into the clouds your visibility is reduced to five meters and your cockpit is covered with rain and/or ice, but your enemies can't see you (and vice versa of course).

The Ace Combat series has developed over time from a fun game to a full-fledged Combat Flight Action Video Game that also forces you to think about the use of fighter jets.
There is also a nice multiplayer option that provides variety. If that wasn't enough, the many options in the tech tree give you plenty of options to complete each mission to the best of your ability.

[h1]Prologue[/h1]
Our story takes place in a universe somewhat different from ours, but with many similarities, such as having developed, designed and built the same fighter models and military planes as our world. This story takes place on the continent of Usean, a place where we find large cities, and also beautiful natural landscapes, such as beaches, forests, deserts and various other types of landscapes, unfortunately all this exuberance is found, where more than a decade ago in 2001 , there was a great war that affected the entire continent. ^^

A war that involved the Kingdom of Erusea, against the other nations of the continent and ended in an armistice. After the end of the war, the other nations, during their reconstruction process, allied themselves with a large military force from another continent, the Osean Federation, which now has troops on the continent for "protection" of the countries, as well as starting the construction of a huge space elevator in the southwest region of the continent, very close to the border with Erusea, bothering and worrying the leadership of the kingdom. Now it's 2019, with the construction of the space elevator completed, and the continued presence of Osean military troops on the continent, making Erusia decide that the time has come to put an end to this, with a withering strike from they air force that would start to a new large war. ^^

[b]Pros:[/b]
+ An excellent game of military fighters, with the most varied types of aircraft, weapons and twenty missions with different objectives on maps with several kilometers in area, to test the aircraft and skills.
+ Twenty-eight different fighter models, each with its own three special weapon options, plus numerous upgrades that can be used on all, including two fifth generation models.
+ Beautiful graphics during combat, including options such as viewing from the cockpit's point of view, and having the camera follow the last missile fired.
+ Impeccable soundtrack, with some really good songs, which I listened to over and over again.
+ Story despite being shown only from the point of view of our squadron and a few other characters, it is easy to understand.

[b]Cons:[/b]
- If you plan to unlock all the planes and upgrades, you need to be patient to collect all the necessary points, as there will be many.
- Some achievements require a lot of repetition, such as completing all quests on all difficulty settings. In addition to achievements that can only be achieved in online mode.
- The game has a considerable amount of DLC, including several aircraft that could have been in the base game but are DLC-exclusive.

[h1] Game mechanics[/h1]
This is how the player's participation begins as a fighter pilot, of one of the divisions of the Osean Federation stationed on the continent of Usean, being awakened by a call to battle on the first day of the invasion by the troops of the Kingdom of Erusea, as the novice and "very communicative" pilot Trigger, performing various types of missions, such as shooting down targets in the air, destroying installations on the ground, protecting allies, among several other types of military operations, throughout the twenty missions of the story mode portraying the war. ^^

In addition, the story starts with only one model of aircraft and a special weapon released, but as the missions are carried out, the player earns points, which can be accumulated to exchange them for more options of special weapons, improvements that can be used in any aircraft, and new fighter models, including a fifth-generation US and Russian fighter, to soar through the skies and shoot down enemies. But be careful, even when piloting the best fighters, the bosses still provide an excellent challenge, especially on the highest difficulties. ^^

[h1] Art and sound[/h1]
Produced by the Japanese studio Bandai Namco, I really liked the graphics of the world and the units on land and sea, but mainly in the modeling of the various fighters, which are the focus of the game after all, with the player piloting them throughout the duration. But the highlight really goes to the sound part, with good sound effects but mainly an impeccable soundtrack, with great songs that even get muffled when we are inside a cloud, some that I kept repeating the mission several times to hear again. ^^

[h1] Conclusion[/h1]
Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown was my first contact with any title in the series, I admit that I had never played an Ace Combat, but I really liked what I saw in this one and I just think it's a shame that I don't have more missions to do, so I can only repeat the missions to try to get the best possible score. Anyway, for those who like military plane games, especially fighters, this is a game that I strongly recommend, whether you are experienced or just like me, a newcomer to the series. I would also be very grateful if Bandai wants to release a sequel one day. ^^

Ace Combat has never been about realism. Let's be honest, enemy planes can literally turn on a dime and infuriatingly break away from tracking weapons with ease whenever it suits them. No airframe should be able to handle what this game does to them, but that isn't the point. Ace Combat has always been about telling a story in a strange world where aerial combat is akin to arturian legends about epic clashings of steel and magic. It seeks to make you feel like a hero, and by god does it pull it off. At worst you'll be evading missiles and taking pot shots at targets, at its best you are the razor that cuts the sky, and every target falls to pieces in your wake in glorious fireballs. All while sweeping music blasts in your ears, mixing with the constant threat of "MISSILE" blaring in your hud. 

The story will always be a subjective thing, and Ace Combat has never been without a healthy helping of cheese, but it's oh so charming. You'll grow attached to your fellow pilots, and you'll grow to laugh at, and swear at both them and your enemies.

The Ace Combat series is the pinnacle of aircraft games, the game-play is dramatic and entertaining, the plot and lore are complex and well thought out, the cut-scenes are incredibly cinematic and the soundtrack is easily the greatest of any game series. The Ace Combat series borders on being a fantasy game, in a fictional universe with princesses and super weapons you are a mute pilot flying with little regard for physics and a celebrated reputation as an ace. Ace Combat 7, the most visually impressive of the series, is a lovely addition that does not disappoint in any regard.

Ace Combat 7 is an amazing game aswell as a good return-to-form for Project Aces. One thing I like the most is the gameplay, no doubt out of all the Ace Combat games I've played Skies Unknown has the absolute best. It's as intense and high-octane as running from a guard dog, the only difference being it's actually fun. But everything else is sort of lacking, and pales in comparison to the older games. The story is kinda... Meh. I loved the whole suicide-squad-esque story it had going on during the 444 missions, but everything after that started to get kind of dull. The DLC missions are wonderful though, my personal favorite being Anchorhead Raid. The soundtrack is good albeit kind of boring (even Daredevil. They use the Daredevil motif in a bunch of the songs here and it gets boring very quickly. Or well, atleast in my experience), that is except Magic Spear! Magic Spear is absolutely amazing and I love it with all my heart.

The multiplayer... Oh boy. 
There is absolutely nothing to love about the multiplayer. It's simple and it's sort of unbalanced. Don't get me wrong, I have fun on the multiplayer every now and then. And if you put in enough time and effort you CAN be as good as the Su-37 guy who keeps one-shotting and out-maneuvering you. It took me like, what, 50 or so hours to get past that level. The point is, the multiplayer is just bad. Downright bad. But it CAN be fun, and I do have fun.

Do I recommend? Yes. Absolutely. But what I recommend even more is to wait for a sale. And who knows, maybe after playing this game you might get an itch to play the older games. My recommendation? Please play The Unsung War.
